title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
abstract: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In a hypothetical graduate course called AI for Scientific Discovery, we would ask how an agent can move beyond producing plausible ideas toward developing testable investigations. Today's lecture is on Discovery R-S-I. Recent work such as Accelerating Scientific Discovery with Co-Scientist and Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement reflects a trend toward agents that generate and organize research ideas. This paper adds a focus on carrying lessons from one research process into later ones. I see your hand, Noah; go ahead.
segments.zh: 在一门假设叫“AI for Scientific Discovery”的研究生课程里，我们会问：一个智能体怎样才能不只是提出看似合理的想法，而是进一步形成可检验的研究。今天的课讲的是Discovery R-S-I。最近的工作，比如Accelerating Scientific Discovery with Co-Scientist和Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement，反映了一个趋势：让智能体生成并组织研究想法。这篇论文还额外关注如何把一个研究过程中的经验带到后续研究中。诺亚，我看到你举手了，请讲。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor, what does it mean to preserve the research process rather than just its final hypothesis?
segments.zh: 教授您好，保留研究过程而不是只保留最终假设，这是什么意思？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It means treating a hypothesis as more than a sentence. A useful, testable proposal connects a claim to evidence, lays out how to investigate it, specifies what results would count for or against it, and considers alternative explanations. Those pieces make the proposal assessable and revisable; they do not make the claim true. Discovery R-S-I keeps versions of these proposals and records how they relate, so later feedback can address the development, not only the final wording.
segments.zh: 这意味着要把假设看得比一句话更重。一个有用、可检验的提案会把主张和证据连起来，说明怎么去研究它，明确什么结果算支持、什么算反对，还会考虑其他可能的解释。这些内容让提案可以被评估、被修改，但并不会让主张本身变成真的。Discovery R-S-I 会保留这些提案的各个版本，并记录它们之间的关系，这样后来的反馈就能针对整个发展过程，而不只是最后的措辞。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: does a compiled investigation mean the proposed science has already been tested?
segments.zh: 快速问一下：一个编译好的调查是否意味着所提出的科学已经经过测试了？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. The research tree records successive hypothesis versions, with links to earlier versions; some revisions may combine more than one parent. Different agents have distinct roles: one selects directions, others generate or repair proposals, critique scientific merit, or assess progress relative to a proposal’s ancestry. Selected computational plans can be compiled into tasks with inputs, environments, outputs, and checks. Compilation shows that a plan is specified for execution, not that it has run or confirmed the hypothesis.
segments.zh: 不是。研究树记录的是各个假设的 successive 版本，并链接到更早的版本；有些修订可能合并了不止一个父版本。不同智能体承担不同角色：一个负责选择方向，其他智能体负责生成或修复提案、评审科学价值，或相对于提案的谱系评估进展。被选中的计算方案可以编译成任务，包含输入、环境、输出和检查。编译只说明方案已经被明确到可执行的程度，并不代表它已经运行过或验证了假设。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The system’s learning loop uses these records to connect assessments with documented contributions. In hypothesis-credit optimization, evidence about a proposal and its development helps assign bounded credit to supported agent actions, which become training targets. A separate process, harness replay, examines recurring workflow failures while holding model weights fixed, then tests targeted changes under matched development conditions. Rediscovery applies accepted changes to fresh questions. The acceptance step can keep the model, the workflow, both, or neither.
segments.zh: 系统的学习循环利用这些记录把评估与有据可查的贡献关联起来。在假设贡献优化中，关于某个提案及其开发过程的证据有助于把有限的功劳分配给有支撑的智能体动作，这些动作随后成为训练目标。另一个独立流程是执行框架回放，它在保持模型权重不变的情况下检查反复出现的工作流故障，然后在匹配的开发条件下测试针对性改动。再发现则把已接受的改动应用到全新问题上。接受这一步可以保留模型、保留工作流、两者都保留，或两者都不保留。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How can the system tell which contribution deserves credit when several agents and revisions are involved?
segments.zh: 当涉及多个智能体和多次修订时，系统如何判断哪一份贡献应当获得奖励？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That is exactly why provenance matters, but the records should not be mistaken for perfect causal attribution. The system uses documented contributions and assessments to select supported histories for training, rather than rewarding every action associated with a successful final score. A useful analogy is reviewing a lab notebook: it helps identify which steps were relevant, yet the record alone cannot prove that one step caused the outcome. The paper’s approach makes feedback more specific, while leaving credit assignment as a methodological challenge.
segments.zh: 这正是溯源之所以重要的原因，但不能把这些记录误当成完美的因果归因。系统利用有据可查的贡献和评估来挑选有支撑的历史用于训练，而不是对与最终成功得分相关的每一个动作都给予奖励。一个有用的类比是审阅实验记录本：它有助于识别哪些步骤是相关的，但仅凭记录无法证明某一步骤导致了该结果。论文的方法让反馈更具体，同时把功劳分配留作一个方法论上的挑战。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A second contribution is a measurement framework called D-F-M Bench. It evaluates five kinds of objects: individual hypotheses, parent-child revisions, ordered development paths, complete research runs, and scientific-contribution families. The distinction matters because one proposal’s quality is not the same as the quality of its revision history or a complete run. The benchmark also separates delivery maturity from scientific quality, so a runnable plan is not automatically treated as a supported scientific contribution.
segments.zh: 第二个贡献是一个叫D-F-M Bench的测量框架。它评估五类对象：单个假设、父子修订、有序的开发路径、完整的研究运行，以及科学贡献家族。这个区分很重要，因为一个提案的质量不等同于它的修订历史或一次完整运行的质量。这个基准还把交付成熟度和科学质量分开，所以一个可运行的计划不会自动被视为有支撑的科学贡献。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Can you clarify what the main quality results actually show, rather than what the system aims to do?
segments.zh: 你能不能讲清楚主要的质量结果到底说明了什么，而不是这个系统打算做什么？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Across 241 research questions in four life-science domains, an automated grader rated hypothesis quality on a 1 to 10 scale across eight dimensions. The weighted average rose from 4.86 for the base model to 5.18 after the first round and 5.39 after the second. The largest gains were in falsifiability, from 4.00 to 6.20, and data resolvability, from 3.73 to 4.99. These scores assess proposal quality, not truth or completed discovery.
segments.zh: 在四个生命科学领域的241个研究问题中，一个自动评分器按八个维度以1到10分评估假设质量。加权平均分从基础模型的4.86上升到第一轮后的5.18，第二轮后达到5.39。提升最大的是可证伪性，从4.00升到6.20，以及数据可解析性，从3.73升到4.99。这些分数评估的是提案质量，而非真实性或已完成的发现。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: The score rises overall, but did every dimension improve, and do human reviewers agree?
segments.zh: 总分是上升了，但每个维度都提升了吗，人类评审员也认同吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No: importance fell from 6.48 to 6.04, and novelty from 4.87 to 4.58, so the gains point more clearly to better-specified tests than to more important or original questions. In a separate review of 292 proposals, 27 medically or bioscience-trained reviewers assessed revisions without seeing model identities or automated scores. Mean parent-child change was plus 0.07 for Discovery R-S-I-27B, plus 0.03 for G-P-T-5.6 Sol, and minus 0.01 for G-P-T-6 Luna. These are dependent revisions within research trees, not independent project outcomes.
segments.zh: 没有：重要性从6.48降到6.04，新颖性从4.87降到4.58，所以这些提升更明显地指向测试设计得更明确，而不是问题更重要或更有原创性。在另一项针对292份提案的评审中，27名受过医学或生物科学训练的评审员在看不到模型身份或自动评分的情况下评估了修订稿。Discovery R-S-I-27B的平均父子变化为加0.07，G-P-T-5.6 Sol为加0.03，G-P-T-6 Luna为减0.01。这些是研究树内的依赖修订，不是独立项目的结果。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The broader connection is that iterative hypothesis generation is not new. Co-Scientist already combines generation, critique, comparison, and refinement, while ScienceBuddy also describes coupled improvement of a model and its research workflow. Discovery R-S-I’s more specific emphasis is retaining evidence and contribution histories across investigations, then using assessments to shape training targets and workflow changes. That focus makes the path from critique to later behavior more explicit, but it does not by itself show which part of the learning loop produced the measured gains.
segments.zh: 更广泛的联系在于，迭代式假设生成并不新鲜。Co-Scientist 已经结合了生成、批判、比较和精炼，而 ScienceBuddy 也描述了模型及其研究工作流的耦合改进。Discovery R-S-I 更具体的重点是在多次调查中保留证据和贡献历史，然后利用评估来塑造训练目标和工作流变更。这一重点使从批判到后续行为的路径更加明确，但它本身并不能说明学习循环的哪一部分产生了所测得的增益。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So what experiment would help establish whether credit optimization, workflow replay, or rediscovery is responsible for the improvement?
segments.zh: 那么，什么实验有助于确定是信用优化、工作流回放还是重新发现带来了改进？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Ablations that isolate those components would help answer that question, alongside evaluation on fresh research questions and careful tracking of dependencies between revisions. The reported base-to-round-two increase accompanies a system combining credit-weighted training, harness replay, and rediscovery; it does not isolate their individual effects. The authors also report shifts toward more evolution and repair and fewer restarts, but operation frequency alone does not establish that any one strategy caused better research.
segments.zh: 要回答这个问题，需要做消融实验来分离这些组件的作用，同时还要在新颖的研究问题上进行评估，并仔细追踪各次修订之间的依赖关系。报告中从基线到第二轮的增长，对应的是一个结合了信用加权训练、框架回放和重新发现的系统；这并不能分离出各个组件的独立效果。作者还报告了向更多演化和修复、更少重启的转变，但仅凭操作频率并不能证明是某一种策略带来了更好的研究。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The key takeaway is that preserving how a testable question develops creates a route for feedback to influence later work. Yet a better-specified proposal remains a proposal. This paper reaches concrete hypotheses and compiled plans; executing those plans, assessing supportive, negative, or inconclusive outcomes, and validating wet-lab claims remain future work. The useful next question is not only whether agents can propose research, but how well their records help us learn from what happens next. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 关键要点在于，保留一个可检验问题的发展过程，能为反馈影响后续工作创造一条路径。然而，一个表述更完善的提案仍然只是提案。这篇论文得出了具体假设并编译了计划；执行这些计划、评估支持性、负面或无定论的结果，以及验证湿实验室的主张，仍是未来的工作。有用的下一个问题不仅是智能体能否提出研究，还包括它们的记录能在多大程度上帮助我们从事后发生的事情中学习。感谢收听。如果你还有任何问题，请询问我们的人工智能助手或留言评论。
